To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most successful programs for teaching individuals with autism to function independently in the community are those that are based in natural environments, are conducted in the context of real-life activities, and are implemented by trained staff who are familiar to the individuals with whom they work and who are able to provide the support needed for the individuals to be successful.

(1) the most effective teaching methods for students with autism involve the use of naturalistic, incidental, and embedded instruction; (2) students with autism can learn a wide variety of academic skills in the natural environment; (3) students with autism learn best from adults who are highly motivated to teach them, who are sensitive to their needs, and who use positive reinforcement; and (4) students with autism are capable of learning in a wide range of community settings.

(a) the most important factor in the success of any program is a well-trained teacher; (b) programs that use the least restrictive environment and naturalistic teaching methods are the most effective; (c) the best programs are those that are based on a solid understanding of the nature of autism and the characteristics of the students; and (d) the best programs include a variety of teaching techniques that are used flexibly and are based on the individual characteristics of the student.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most effective and efficient teaching methods for students with autism.
the development of effective teaching methods for the education of students with autism in natural environments.
the development of educational procedures that will enable students with autism to learn to function in a variety of community environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a dearth of empirical data on the teaching of students with autism in natural settings.
the research literature is inadequate for the development of educational programming for students with autism.
the literature in the area of autism does not adequately provide the information necessary to enable educators to teach students with this disability to function in natural community environments.

we have found that students with autism can be taught in natural environments, and that they can be taught to function in these environments with a high degree of independence.
the current research base does not provide a sufficient basis for educators to design programs to prepare students with autism for a range of community environments.
the current research literature is inadequate to guide the development of effective community-based educational programs for students with autism.

we need to focus on the development of a comprehensive curriculum that will enable students to develop skills in a number of different areas that will be useful to them in a variety of settings.
